question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -11 & -5 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & -1 & 5 \\ -3 & -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{22}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{22}=2$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -11 & -5 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & -1 & 5 \\ -3 & -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 4 & 7 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 4 & 7 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 7 \\ 8 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 7 \\ 8 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
